title: Incompatible Timeline Interval Boundaries (Timeline Alignment)
damaged_code:
```rust
fn plot_compare(source_a: &[Event], source_b: &[Event]) {
    let timeline_a = aggregate_to_buckets(source_a, Duration::from_secs(3)); // 3M years
    let timeline_b = aggregate_to_buckets(source_b, Duration::from_secs(15)); // 15M years
    render_side_by_side(timeline_a, timeline_b); // Direct visual comparison of raw heights
}
```
pattern: Plotting or comparing counts per interval on a timeline where the time-slices (bucket widths) differ between datasets.
why_bad: Directly comparing raw heights is mathematically distorted. A peak of "50 events per 15 million years" looks much smaller than "17 events per 1 million years" if plotted without normalization. Users will visually misinterpret the data, completely missing critical density bursts.
detection: Rendering timelines of different datasets without normalizing the Y-axis to a common base rate (e.g., events per second).
strength: Strong` — visually distorts relative frequency metrics by factors equal to the bucket size ratios.
source: Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Chapter 9.3, p. 143/144.
